item.title: Keep Her Centred in Portrait

turns.text: Make this landscape clip vertical, 9:16. Keep her centred throughout and keep the full 10 seconds with the original sound. No captions.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing of existing footage while preserving the speaker, duration and source audio.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4 and keep the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Framing style: Crop to fill the frame without stretching; keep her face and head comfortably visible.
answer_sheet.Audio and text: Keep the original speech and sound. No captions or other added text.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 video using the attached woman's actual footage, not a newly generated recreation.
The woman remains horizontally centred with her face and head comfortably visible throughout.
The picture fills the portrait frame without stretching or black bars.
The full 10-second sequence and original speech are retained in sync.
No captions or other text have been added.

turns.text: Could you turn this landscape clip into a vertical version for me? I’m a little worried about how it will look when the framing changes. What I mean is a 9:16 version, keeping the full 10 seconds rather than shortening it. Please keep the woman centred throughout the clip. Keep the original sound, and don’t add any captions.

dialog.agent:
A **9:16 tracked crop** is the right approach: it keeps the full 10 seconds and follows the woman so she stays centred, without regenerating the footage or changing the sound.

The connected tools don’t offer a precise crop/reframe operation, so I can’t reliably produce that version here while preserving your original audio.

For the framing you’re worried about, landscape-to-portrait cropping removes a lot from both sides. In a video editor, use:
- A **9:16 canvas** and all **10 seconds**
- Subject tracking/auto-reframe on the woman, correcting the crop position with keyframes where needed
- The **original audio unchanged**, with captions off

Preview her widest gestures before exporting—those are most likely to get cut off. If necessary, slightly shrink the footage over a blurred background to retain more of the scene.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
I tried the full 10-second edit, but Magic Hour refused it because your account has **insufficient credits**. No video was generated.

I haven’t shortened the clip or changed your requirements. For this particular job, a standard editor’s **9:16 auto-reframe/subject-tracking** feature would be the better option: it can keep the woman centred while retaining all 10 seconds and the original sound, with captions off.

approvals.name: edit_video

style.prompt: Reframe this landscape clip into a vertical portrait 9:16 video. Preserve the entire original 10-second duration, original timing and sequence without shortening, speeding up, or omitting any footage. Keep the woman centered throughout by smoothly tracking her position with the crop, keeping her face and gestures visible where possible. Only change framing: preserve the original woman, appearance, actions, scene and lighting without adding or changing content. Keep the original source audio unchanged throughout, including all speech and background sounds; do not generate replacement speech, music or sounds. Do not add any captions, subtitles, text, logos or overlays.
